body:
## Summary
Thirteen numbers that TypeScript and the Python pipeline must agree on (scorecard notes budget, screening-volume tiers, calibration bins and floor, interview-kit caps, letter cap, probe threshold, fit floors) are typed twice and held together by three test modules that each carry a private regex parser of TypeScript. Generate them from Python through the codegen door that already exists, and re-point the sync tests at the door instead of at the literals.

## Description
This context owns test_automation_constant_sync.py, whose MIRRORED map is the list of places the repo broke its own rule (api-contracts.md §2.3: do not hand-write a TypeScript mirror). Every new cross-language number today costs a new regex extractor with its own blind spots; five near-identical copies of `_strip_ts_comments` exist across the suite. codegen.py already emits policy numbers (the devcase timebox bounds) into taxonomy.generated.ts for exactly this reason. The move: a `CONTRACT_CONSTANTS` table in codegen.py (TS name -> Python module attribute), a `render_contract_constants()` renderer registered in `_GENERATED`, an import-free `app/_lib/contract-constants.generated.ts`, and each of the 7 TS modules replacing its literal with `export { NAME } from "./contract-constants.generated"` (names unchanged, so no consumer moves). The three sync modules keep every behavioural non-vacuity probe and swap the literal-equality half for 'the TS module re-exports from the generated file and declares no literal'; a new test pins the committed generated file against the renderer, because CI never runs schemas:check.

## Flow
1. codegen.py: CONTRACT_CONSTANTS table + render_contract_constants() + _GENERATED row; header names the Python sources.
2. Run codegen; commit the generated file; add test_codegen_contract_constants.py (render, patched-value derivation, freshness, --check, import-free, bad-row).
3. Switch the 7 TS modules to re-exports, keeping their doc comments (now pointing at the generator).
4. Re-point test_automation_constant_sync / test_fit_threshold_sync / test_devcase_probe_constant_sync: literal-equality -> re-export assertion; keep every behavioural probe; delete no test method (review:constitution counts deletions).
5. api-contracts.md §2.3 lists the third generated file.

## Expected impact
The 13-number drift class closes by construction rather than by detection; a new shared number costs one table row, not one more parser. Three copies of the TS comment-stripper leave the suite. The generated file is also freshness-pinned in a CI lane for the first time (schemas:check is not a CI step).

## Evaluation
Claim: every hand-mirrored contract number has one source (Python) and the TS side can no longer carry a divergent literal.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - test_codegen_contract_constants.py + the three re-pointed sync modules under npm run test:python:gate; npx tsc --noEmit; npm run test:unit (TS consumers of the names)
Result: pending build
Gate: contract
evidence: grep 'export const <NAME>' over the 7 TS files: interview-transcript.ts:57 MAX_SCORECARD_NOTES_CHARS = 6000; automation-cache-key.ts:62 SCREEN_VOLUME_SPARSE_MAX = 5, :63 SCREEN_VOLUME_MODERATE_MAX = 30; calibration.ts:15 MIN_CALIBRATION_OUTCOMES = 20, :18 CALIBRATION_BIN_COUNT = 10; interview-kit-types.ts:30-33 KIT_MAX_* = 8/6/5/12; interview-letter-types.ts:76 LETTER_MAX_CHARS = 2400; devcase-probe-audit.ts:49 MIN_PROBE_DECISION_OPTIONS = 2; fit-thresholds.ts:13 FIT_PROMISING_FLOOR = 55, :23 FIT_STRONG_FLOOR = 70. Python: matching.py:80 FIT_STRONG_THRESHOLD = 70, :81 FIT_PROMISING_THRESHOLD = 55; devcase/design.py:98 MIN_PROBE_DECISION_OPTIONS = 2; automation.py:161-162 POLICY screen_volume 5/30, :1485-1488 KIT_MAX_*, :1846 LETTER_MAX_CHARS = 2400, :2361 MAX_SCORECARD_NOTES_CHARS = 6000; calibration_drift.py:40-41. grep 'def _strip_ts_comments' pipeline/jobfit/tests: test_analysis_prompt_version_sync.py:161, test_automation_constant_sync.py:80, test_devcase_probe_constant_sync.py:36, test_fit_threshold_sync.py:41, test_prompt_version_sync.py:84 = 5 copies. codegen.py:175-181 already renders DEVCASE_MAX_TIMEBOX_HOURS / DEVCASE_MIN_TIMEBOX_HOURS. package.json:29 schemas:check; ci.yml mentions schemas only in comments (:33) and the pip-install step name (:49). Context owners: test_fit_threshold_sync.py -> tests-scoring-fairness, test_devcase_probe_constant_sync.py -> tests-devcase, codegen.py -> pipeline-core (no prior challenge card on any of them).

title: Skip gate by identity: a skip register that names the new skip and the stale one
acceptance: evaluate_skips(skipped=[(A,'r')], register={A: always}, baseline=1) -> exit 0, report lists A as tolerated with its register `why`

SUBSTITUTION: register {A: env-conditional, B: always, C..E: always} baseline 5; run where A RAN and a new Y skipped (count 5, inside today's 4-5 band) -> exit 1, stderr names Y, its skip reason, and 'not in pipeline/jobfit/tests/skip-register.json' (today's count gate exits 0)
LOCAL HOLE: full checkout where the env-conditional A runs (count 4) plus one brand-new skip Y (count 5 <= ceiling) -> exit 1 naming Y (today exits 0)
an `always` entry B that did not skip -> exit 1: 'stale register entry B ran - delete it and set KP_SKIP_BASELINE to N-1 in .github/workflows/ci.yml' (the remedy names the exact edit)
an env-conditional entry A that ran -> exit 0 with a one-line note, never a failure
len(register) != KP_SKIP_BASELINE -> exit 1 naming both numbers BEFORE the suite runs, so the register cannot grow without the env raise review:constitution already blocks

a register entry whose id is not a discovered test id, or whose `why` is under 20 characters -> exit 1 as dead/unexplained, checked before the suite runs (same rule test-quarantine.json applies to node tests)
ALLOW_SKIP=1 -> exit 0 regardless (local keyless override unchanged); hermeticity tripwire still runs first
premise: pipeline/jobfit/tests/run_gated.py:52 SKIP_BASELINE and :67 ENV_CONDITIONAL_SKIPS - the gate holds a COUNT; :193-221 compares len(result.skipped) to a floor/ceiling band and never looks at which tests skipped

pipeline/jobfit/tests/run_gated.py:54-66 - the floor is ceiling-1 because one tolerated skip runs in a full checkout, so locally a brand-new silent skip fits inside the band (4 tolerated + 1 new = 5 <= ceiling)
pipeline/jobfit/tests/run_gated.py:205-211 - the over-ceiling message says only 'A critical test may be silently skipping. Investigate' - it prints the list but cannot say which entry is the new one
.github/workflows/ci.yml:404-438 - the identity of the tolerated skips lives only as a hand-kept comment derivation keyed on file:line

that derivation has already drifted: ci.yml:420 says test_interview_eval.py:574 (skipTest is at :579); :428 test_llm_base.py:409,:475 (now :515,:581); :429 test_llm_self_host.py:124 (now :119); :433 test_repo_scan.py:243,:526 (now :264,:547)

docs/development/testing-and-evaluation.md:187-191 - 'The Python suite (test:python:gate) has its own pawl - the KP_SKIP_BASELINE skip count - and no flake classification' - an admitted gap beside the identity-keyed test-quarantine.json the node suite already has

scripts/review/constitution-check.mjs:169 lists run_gated.py as a gate-policy file; :516/:572 block a raised KP_SKIP_BASELINE - the register must join that category so its growth stays reviewer-visible
rollback: Revert the commit series: run_gated.py returns to the count band, the register and its test file are deleted, ci.yml regains its comment derivation. KP_SKIP_BASELINE is never changed by this card, so the constitution lens and release.yml:95 are unaffected either way.
runner_up: Turn --timings from a report into a per-module wall-clock ceiling (a module budget file with a ratchet), so the slowest-module list in CI stops being advisory - smaller operator payoff, and ci:budget already holds the job-level ceiling.
body:
## Summary
The gated Python suite decides by counting skips, so a new silent skip that replaces a tolerated one - or that arrives in a full checkout where one tolerated skip runs - passes green, and the tripwire, when it does fire, can only say 'investigate'. Replace the count with a committed skip register keyed by test id: the gate names the unexpected skip, names the stale entry, and names the exact edit.

## Description
The operator surface here is the gate's own output (run_gated.py is what an agent or the owner reads when test:python:gate goes red). Today the identity of the five tolerated skips lives as a ci.yml comment keyed on file:line, and four of those line numbers are already wrong. The card adds `pipeline/jobfit/tests/skip-register.json` (entries: test id, `why`, `when`: always | env-conditional, the condition text), and splits run_gated's verdict into a pure `evaluate_skips(skipped, register, baseline, discovered_ids)` so every branch is unit-testable. KP_SKIP_BASELINE stays and must equal the register length, so growing the register still requires the env raise that review:constitution blocks - the count gate is kept as a second lock, not replaced by a looser one. The ci.yml derivation comment shrinks to a pointer at the register; constitution-check adds the register to its gate-policy file category.

## Flow
1. Write test_run_gated.py against evaluate_skips (all 8 cases red).
2. Add skip-register.json with the five current ids, whys and conditions (read from the actual skip sites, not from the drifted comment).
3. Implement evaluate_skips + pre-run register validation (dead id, short why, length != baseline); main() calls it after the hermeticity check.
4. ci.yml comment -> pointer; constitution-check.mjs category row + fixture case.
5. testing-and-evaluation.md: replace the 'own pawl' sentence with the register's rules.

## Expected impact
A silent skip can no longer hide by substitution or in a developer checkout; the red message tells the reader which test and which edit, instead of a count and 'investigate'. The hand-kept file:line derivation that has already rotted is retired.

## Evaluation
Claim: the Python gate identifies each skip by test id and refuses any skip the register does not name, while keeping the KP_SKIP_BASELINE lock.
Before: 0 of 8 acceptance cases pass
After: 8 of 8
Method: gate - test_run_gated.py in npm run test:python:gate; npm run test:review for the constitution fixture; a real run of test:python:gate stays green with the 5 registered skips
Result: pending build
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: run_gated.py:194 floor = max(0, SKIP_BASELINE - ENV_CONDITIONAL_SKIPS); :205 `if skipped > SKIP_BASELINE`; :212 `if skipped < floor` - only len(result.skipped) is compared. ci.yml:440 KP_SKIP_BASELINE: "5"; release.yml:95 same. Drift check (grep -n skipTest/skipUnless): test_interview_eval.py:579 'grounded DB-fixture bridge unavailable' vs ci.yml:420 ':574'; test_llm_base.py:515,:581 vs ci.yml:428 ':409,:475'; test_llm_self_host.py:119 vs ci.yml:429 ':124'; test_repo_scan.py:264,:419,:547,:559,:899 vs ci.yml ':243,:526 / :398 / :538 / :825'. test-quarantine.json already keys node flakes by file+test with why/since/expires; testing-and-evaluation.md:187-191 names the Python side's lack of it. Prior decks: no skip/register card in any challenge-*/cards; leftover-develop has only the unrelated node 'Treat test.skipIf as a skip marker'.
